text:
maria: heads up — the new sample app's telemetry hooks aren't carrying request IDs into background workers. debug logs show different reqids for the http handler vs the queued job.

sam: ugh thanks for spotting. is this node or python sample?

maria: node. stack: express -> enqueue job to bullmq -> worker picks it up. we init open-telemetry via the sdk autoinstrumentation and also attach a req-id middleware that sets X-Request-Id. example init: ```js
const { registerInstrumentations } = require('@opentelemetry/instrumentation');
registerInstrumentations({ instrumentations: [/* http, express */] });
app.use((req,res,next)=>{ req.id = req.headers['x-request-id'] || uuid(); res.setHeader('X-Request-Id', req.id); next(); });
```
but the worker logs start with a new uuid.

jordan: does the enqueue call preserve headers? many queues don't. are you explicitly passing req id in job payload?

maria: right now we assume OTEL context propagation handles it. didn't pass in payload. that's on me but wondering if SDK should make this easier — parity with python sample seems better. in python sample (older), celery tasks pulled request id from current_context via otel and it worked. node autoinstrumentation seems not to propagate across async boundaries for our queue setup.

sam: opened a quick issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/439 — sketching a fix to export a helper `captureJobContext(job, req)` that copies trace/span/reqid into job.meta. can we add a devex sample that shows both explicit and implicit approaches?

ian: one more wrinkle — in our dedicated env the ingress nginx strips unknown headers unless whitelisted. so even if the app sets X-Request-Id, it might be gone before hitting the worker cluster. check the proxy header whitelist: `nginx.conf -> proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;` if missing we lose it. saw this last week in staging.

aleks: for redaction: node SDK currently applies secret redaction only at INFO+ levels, and debug logs bypass the sanitizers (intended to keep developer visibility). that bites: debug shows tokens. we should either always redact secrets or provide a dev flag `debug_safe=true`. proposed config: ```json
{ "log_level": "debug", "redact_secrets": true, "debug_safe": true }
```
this would run a light-weight scrubber even for debug.

maria: yeah we accidentally logged a user token in dev logs. panic avoided but we need to change sample for onboarding.

sam: agreed. plan: (1) add helper to copy reqid into job.payload.meta, (2) add docs snippet for nginx header whitelist, (3) toggle debug-safe redaction in samples, (4) ensure parity tests between node/python samples. I can take (1) and (3). anyone own nginx docs?

ian: i'll update the infra doc. will add a note about header preservation and a small config snippet for k8s ingress.

jordan: +1 on parity tests. maybe a tiny e2e that fires a request, enqueues, and asserts the same request id in worker logs. keep it short.

maria: thanks — i'm pushing a minimal repro to the sample-app repo now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/222 (WIP). ping me if you want to pair on the worker wrapper. :eyes:

devex-bot: CI | sample-apps PR 222 — 3 checks running: lint, unit, telemetry-e2e.

sam: nice. once PR lands i'll add the sdk helper and a follow-up patch to toggle debug-safe redaction by default in samples.

aleks: i'll prepare a tiny scrubber util and a benchmark — impact should be <1% on log throughput. will paste results in the PR. :bug:

maria: great, leaving the thread open for reviews. thanks all!
